prompt:
Research Docker Hub's officially documented pull rate limits for unauthenticated and authenticated free users. Cite Docker's documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, there is a discrepancy between Docker's official documentation pages and their recent blog/FAQ announcements regarding the pull rate limits for free users. The core documentation still reflects a 6-hour limit, while newer policy updates and FAQs mention an hourly limit that was scheduled but then delayed/unenforced.

Here are the officially documented limits along with the exact quotes and citations:

SOURCE: https://docs.docker.com/docker-hub/usage/pulls/ | QUOTE: "Unauthenticated and Docker Personal users are subject to a 6-hour pull rate limit on Docker Hub." | CLAIM: The pull rate limits for both unauthenticated and authenticated free (Personal) users are calculated on a 6-hour window.

SOURCE: https://docs.docker.com/docker-hub/usage/ | QUOTE: "Personal (authenticated) | 200" | CLAIM: The documented pull rate limit for authenticated free (Docker Personal) users is 200 pulls per 6 hours.

SOURCE: https://docs.docker.com/docker-hub/usage/ | QUOTE: "Unauthenticated users | 100 per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet" | CLAIM: The documented pull rate limit for unauthenticated users is 100 pulls per 6 hours per IP address/subnet.

SOURCE: https://www.docker.com/pricing/faq/ | QUOTE: "For authenticated Personal users, there is a 100 pull/hour rate limit per user; for unauthenticated users, there is a 10 pull/hour rate limit per IP address." | CLAIM: Docker's pricing FAQ documents an hourly rate limit policy (100 pulls/hour for authenticated Personal users, 10 pulls/hour for unauthenticated users).

SOURCE: https://www.docker.com/blog/revisiting-docker-hub-policies-prioritizing-developer-experience/ | QUOTE: "We did not enforce the Docker Hub rate limit changes previously scheduled for April 1, 2025. The current limits—100 pulls per 6 hours for unauthenticated users and 200 pulls per 6 hours for Docker Personal users—will remain in place" | CLAIM: As of April 8, 2025, the officially enforced limits remain the original 6-hour limits (100 per 6 hours for unauthenticated, 200 per 6 hours for Personal) because the announced hourly limits were not enforced.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: An updated official documentation page (docs.docker.com) explicitly reflecting the April 2025 enforcement delay or officially replacing the 6-hour limits with the hourly limits in the core usage tables.
